rule: good. the rule string is context only and is never parsed; texts 2 and 3 are fine as written, while texts 1 and 4 need the rewrites below.
texts: bad: 'the neighboring stations' is a definite plural, so the translator handed the requesting down to each member of that group and never recorded that the stations requested anything as a body — and because no station is ever declared a member of the group, nothing derives from the sentence at all. Range over the stations one at a time instead: 'When wraith activity at the Sunken Cove increases, each neighboring station requests feather rations from the Council.'

good. the whenever wording gives a fireable per-rise rule covering the sightings, the Sunken Cove, the stations, the Council and the requested rations; a reviewer objection about how the sightings are located was examined and rejected.
good. one plain event with the Council, the requests and the central feather store all covered, and the compound correctly unpacked.

bad: 'stations with drained lanterns' has no supported reading for 'with', so the translator turned it into a claim that the lanterns sit inside the stations — a spatial fact your sentence never states — and it also recorded the rule as absolute rather than as the general tendency the wording states. Say the relation outright with a relative clause: 'The Council prioritizes stations whose lanterns are drained.' Add 'always' if you do mean it without exception.
